title: {{NAME}} and the Three Forces
moral: Ancient power, modern courage, and timeless magic are all needed in equal measure.

pages.content:
Three things happened simultaneously on the same Tuesday afternoon.

First: a temporal fault opened over the city and a juvenile Triceratops came through, confused and lost.

Second: a unicorn named Aurelius, who had been working with the city hero squad for a year, felt the temporal disruption and arrived at the site before the heroes did.

Third: {{NAME}}, on his way home from school, happened to be standing exactly at the fault site with his hero registration badge in his pocket and absolutely no backup.

He put the badge on.

pages.content:
The immediate priority: the Triceratops was panicking. It charged twice, not aggressively but the way very large animals move when frightened, enormous and uncontrolled.

Aurelius stepped in front of it.

Unicorns, apparently, carried the memory of a time when they and Triceratops had coexisted, and Aurelius emitted a specific frequency from his horn that the Triceratops's ancient instincts recognised as: large, calm, not a threat.

The Triceratops stopped.

Aurelius looked at {{NAME}}: now.

{{NAME}} understood. He had three minutes of calm to work with.

Aurelius the unicorn standing before the Triceratops, horn glowing with the recognition frequency, the Triceratops going still, {{NAME}} already moving with purpose. pages.content:
He used two minutes and forty seconds.

The hero squad arrived at the two-minute mark. {{NAME}} had already set up a soft barrier perimeter using the emergency equipment in the nearby road maintenance box.

The third hero on scene had a temporal containment field. They deployed it around the Triceratops with Aurelius still inside, still keeping it calm.

The field held. The Triceratops was contained, unharmed.

The squad leader looked at the perimeter, then at {{NAME}}.

"How long have you been on scene?"

"About three minutes," said {{NAME}}.

pages.content:
The Triceratops was returned through the repaired fault with Aurelius accompanying it partway, horn maintaining the calming frequency until the creature was through.

{{NAME}} watched the portal close from the perimeter.

Aurelius walked to him and stood before him for a moment, then put his horn briefly to the hero badge on {{NAME}}'s chest.

The squad leader said: "That's an acknowledgement from a unicorn ally. Rare."

"We worked well together," said {{NAME}}.

"He's saying he noticed," she said.

pages.content:
He walked home in the late afternoon light, badge warm on his chest.

He thought about the three minutes: Aurelius's frequency, the dinosaur going still, himself moving into the space that required filling.

Three very different things. Each exactly what the situation needed.

In bed that night, the badge on the bedside table, he closed his eyes.

Somewhere in the city, Aurelius was working with the hero squad on tomorrow's problems.

Somewhere in another time, a Triceratops was home.

He fell asleep warm.
